grand_strategy.reading:
Colombia changed its partner in 2026 without changing its problem: the cocaine economy and the armed groups on the Venezuelan border are the same, and a hard-line Trump ally sworn in on 7 Aug 2026 has bet that Washington's force can do what negotiation did not. The reset reverses the Petro-era rupture (decertification, sanctions on the president, the tariff war with Ecuador), and the energy lever is back in use, while the Belt and Road pact of May 2025 is a non-binding letter that the new government has not yet addressed in any source found. The paradox is that the rupture cost Colombia its aid and its standing, and the reset buys security cooperation at a price that the policy itself may push across the borders, into Venezuela and Ecuador (an inference, not yet sourced).

Added on 16 Oct 2026, after ten weeks of the new government. The reset has two faces. At home, it replaces negotiation with force (four air strikes since 7 Aug, an ultimatum to the Clan del Golfo, extradition and surrender as the exits) and bets that Washington's backing will outlast a 49.66% mandate and a minority in Congress. Abroad, it prices alignment in ideological currency: Israel restored and its embassy moved to Jerusalem, Cuba and Nicaragua cut, the Sahrawi Republic frozen, South Africa's ICJ case abandoned, the Palestine vote abstained, 14 embassies closed. The payoff so far is thin and probationary: a waiver instead of recertification on 16 Sep, Petro still on the SDN list on 7 Oct, and a Venezuela that Washington took off the list while Colombia stayed on it. The test comes within a year, when the coca hectares of 2025 and 2026 will be counted against a promise that supply can be cut by force, and the 2024 data (a 54% fall in forced eradication with the smallest rise in coca area in four years) do not yet say it can. What the new government's line on China, Russia and the Belt and Road letter of May 2025 will be remains unsourced; so does the status of the ELN's Venezuelan sanctuary after the change of government.
